map.subsystem: Core monitoring and display (Android phone app: home dashboard, glucose hero + trend arrow, glucose/IoB/basal/bolus chart, TIR / CGM-stats / insulin-summary / recent-bolus cards, freshness-staleness state machine, status icons, mg/dL↔mmol/L unit handling, theme, and the whole navigation graph)

capabilities.name: Home dashboard composition and vertical order
capabilities.behavior: HomeScreen is a PullToRefreshBox wrapping a vertically-scrolling Column with padding start/end/top = 16.dp and bottom = 88.dp (extra bottom space so the camera FAB never overlaps the last item), horizontally centered. Fixed child order, each separated by a 12.dp Spacer unless noted: (1) ConnectionSyncRow (BLE + sync + backend-reachability icons + plugin brand marks); (2) GlucoseHero; (3) RecentMealCard (only when mealState.recentMeal != null); (4) GlucoseTrendChart (with onClick -> chart detail); (5) TimeInRangeBar; (6) CgmStatsCard; (7) InsulinSummaryCard; (8) RecentBolusesCard; (9) plugin-contributed cards sorted by DashboardCardDescriptor.priority ascending (lower = higher on screen), each preceded by a 12.dp Spacer; (10) 24.dp Spacer; (11) a single footer line: if connectionState == DISCONNECTED -> 'Pair your pump in Settings to start' (onSurfaceVariant); else if connectionState == CONNECTED && cgm == null -> 'Loading pump data...' (tertiary); otherwise nothing. Overlaid in the pull-to-refresh Box (not in the scroll column) is the DraggableMealFab, shown only when backendConfigured && mealState.mealLoggingAvailable. Pull-to-refresh calls viewModel.refreshData() and mealViewModel.refresh(). ON_RESUME re-fetches the recent-meal glance, skipping the first resume (the VM already fetched in init). Container size is captured via onSizeChanged to clamp the draggable FAB.
edge_cases: Plugin cards are re-sorted by priority in the screen even though HomeViewModel already sorted them (double sort, stable behavior).
Every card is always present even with no data; each renders its own empty-state string rather than being hidden.
The FAB is gated at composition on backendConfigured (BLE-only mode hides meal logging entirely — meal analysis is backend-only).

capabilities.name: Status icon row (BLE / sync / backend reachability) — documented in docs/mobile/status-icons.mdx
capabilities.behavior:
ConnectionSyncRow renders a centered Row (testTag 'connection_status') of 16.dp icons.

BLE pump icon (always shown), mapped from ConnectionState:
- CONNECTED -> Icons.Default.BluetoothConnected, a11y 'Pump connected', colorScheme.primary (blue), NO text.
- CONNECTING or AUTHENTICATING -> Icons.AutoMirrored.Filled.BluetoothSearching, a11y 'Connecting to pump', colorScheme.tertiary (amber), text 'Connecting...'.
- RECONNECTING -> Icons.Default.Bluetooth, a11y 'Reconnecting to pump', tertiary, text 'Reconnecting...'.
- SCANNING -> BluetoothSearching, a11y 'Scanning for pump', tertiary, text 'Scanning...'.
- AUTH_FAILED -> Icons.Default.BluetoothDisabled, a11y 'Pump pairing failed', colorScheme.error (red), text 'Pairing failed'.
- DISCONNECTED -> BluetoothDisabled, a11y 'No pump connected', error, NO text.
Icon-to-text gap is 4.dp; text style labelSmall in the same color.

The next two indicators render ONLY when backendConfigured == true (BLE-only users have no cloud, so 'pending sync' / 'reachable' would be claims about a server that does not exist). 12.dp spacer before each.

Sync icon, first matching branch of SyncStatus(lastSyncAtMs, pendingCount, lastError):
- lastError != null -> CloudOff, 'Sync error', error.
- pendingCount > 0 -> CloudSync, '<n> readings pending sync', tertiary.
- lastSyncAtMs > 0 -> Icons.Default.SwapVert (deliberately up/down arrows, NOT a cloud, so the healthy sync state stays visually distinct from the healthy reachability cloud-check — GLY-166), 'Synced to cloud', primary.
- else -> CloudOff, 'Not synced', onSurfaceVariant.
The sync icon never shows text.

BackendStatusIndicator (testTag 'backend_status'), from NetworkStatus:
- REACHABLE -> CloudDone, 'Backend reachable', primary, NO text (quiet golden path).
- BACKEND_UNREACHABLE -> CloudOff, 'Backend unreachable', error, text 'Backend unreachable'.
- OFFLINE -> CloudOff, 'Device offline', error, text 'Offline'.

The published doc states the design intent: two separate icons because sync answers 'is my data uploaded?' and reachability answers 'can I reach the server this instant?'.
edge_cases: The crossed-out Bluetooth icon is explicitly NOT an error state — it is the resting state when no pump is paired/idle/out of range (documented).
Only ONE pump plugin can be active, so at most one pump brand mark is ever shown.

backendConfigured seeds pessimistically false (AuthTokenStore.backendConfiguredFlow() runs on IO because reading the encrypted store on main can block on first keyset load), so the cloud icons can appear a frame late.

capabilities.name: Active-plugin brand indicators
capabilities.behavior: After the status icons, each active plugin with a bundled logo renders its brand mark, untinted (keeps brand colors), inside a Row with Modifier.weight(1f, fill = false).horizontalScroll(...) so a wide badge set can never push the status icons off a narrow screen. Each mark is preceded by a 12.dp spacer and keyed by brand name. Mapping (by stable reverse-domain plugin ID) with per-brand heights normalizing optical weight in the ~16dp row: 'com.glycemicgpt.tandem' -> ic_plugin_tandem, name 'Tandem', height 16.dp; 'com.glycemicgpt.medtronic' -> ic_plugin_medtronic, 'Medtronic', 12.dp; 'com.glycemicgpt.nightscout-source' -> ic_plugin_nightscout, 'Nightscout', 16.dp; anything else -> no badge. contentDescription is '<Name> plugin active'; testTag 'plugin_indicator_<name lowercased>'. IDs come from HomeViewModel.activePluginIds, which maps PluginRegistry.allActivePlugins to IDs and SORTS them, because the registry is backed by a ConcurrentHashMap whose iteration order is undefined and would otherwise let badges shuffle between emissions. Shipping the manufacturer marks was an explicit project-lead decision (nominative use).
edge_cases: A plugin without a bundled logo (e.g. a user-added custom plugin) stays active but shows no mark.
Brand marks are shown in EVERY mode including BLE-only (a BLE-only user still has a pump plugin active).

capabilities.name: Glucose hero (primary value + trend arrow + unit label + freshness + secondary metrics)
capabilities.behavior:
A full-width Card (colorScheme.surface) with 20.dp padding, centered column.

With a reading present:
- Row (bottom-aligned, centered): the glucose number at fontSize 64.sp, FontWeight.Bold (testTag 'glucose_hero_value'), then the trend arrow glyph at 40.sp Bold with padding(bottom = 8.dp, start = 4.dp) (testTag 'glucose_hero_trend'). Both use the SAME color.
- Color = glucoseColor(cgm.glucoseMgDl, thresholds), EXCEPT when the reading is TOO_STALE, in which case both value and arrow render in colorScheme.onSurfaceVariant (de-emphasised grey) so a stale number cannot be mistaken for a confident live reading.
- Below: the unit label ('mg/dL' or 'mmol/L') in bodyMedium/onSurfaceVariant.
- 4.dp spacer, then a Row: the relative-age caption (labelSmall, colored by freshness: FRESH=green InRange, STALE=amber High, TOO_STALE=onSurfaceVariant) and, only when freshness != FRESH, a 6.dp spacer + StalenessBadge.
- Secondary metrics Row (SpaceEvenly, after a 12.dp spacer) rendered only if at least one of iob/basal/battery/reservoir is non-null. Each is a centered column of labelSmall label + bodyMedium SemiBold value, value colored onSurface when FRESH else onSurfaceVariant, plus a 2.dp spacer + StalenessBadge when not FRESH:
  * IoB — label 'IoB', value "%.2fu" of iob.iob (testTag 'hero_iob')
  * Basal — label 'Basal', value "%.2f u/hr" of rate PLUS a mode suffix: PumpActivityMode.SLEEP -> ' Sleep', EXERCISE -> ' Exercise', NONE -> ' Automated' when isAutomated else '' (testTag 'hero_basal')
  * Battery — label 'Battery', value '<pct>%' (testTag 'hero_battery')
  * Reservoir — label 'Reservoir', value "%.0fu" (testTag 'hero_reservoir')
- Freshness policies: the glucose value uses the injected cgmThresholds (default FreshnessPolicy.CGM); ALL four pump metrics use FreshnessPolicy.PUMP.

With no reading: '--' at 64.sp Bold in onSurfaceVariant, plus the unit label. No freshness caption, no badge, no secondary metrics.

Accessibility: the whole card carries one contentDescription. With a reading it is 'Glucose <formatted value> <spoken unit>, <trend name lowercased with underscores replaced by spaces>' then, if TOO_STALE, ', reading is stale, last updated <age label>' inserted BEFORE the metrics, then ', insulin on board %.2f units', ', basal rate %.2f units per hour', ', battery N percent', ', reservoir %.0f units' for each present metric. With no reading: 'No glucose data available'.

Implementation note preserved in code: all five rememberFreshness calls are made unconditionally (using Instant.EPOCH as a stand-in when a value is absent) to keep the composition slot structure stable.
edge_cases: An absent metric with the EPOCH stand-in would classify as TOO_STALE, but the freshness value is only consumed inside the corresponding non-null branch.
The secondary metrics use Kotlin String.format with the DEFAULT locale (not Locale.US), so a comma-decimal device renders '1,23u' — unlike GlucoseFormat which forces Locale.US.
The a11y string appends 'reading is stale' ONLY for TOO_STALE, not for STALE.

capabilities.name: Glucose color banding (thresholds)
capabilities.behavior:
glucoseColor(mgDl, thresholds) — pure function of the STORED mg/dL value; there is no unit parameter, so display-unit choice can never change the severity color:
  mgDl <= urgentLow -> GlucoseColors.UrgentLow
  mgDl <= low       -> GlucoseColors.Low
  mgDl <  high      -> GlucoseColors.InRange
  mgDl <  urgentHigh-> GlucoseColors.High
  else              -> GlucoseColors.UrgentHigh
GlucoseThresholds defaults: urgentLow = 55, low = 70, high = 180, urgentHigh = 250 (matching backend defaults and GlucoseRangeStore defaults). Pinned boundary behavior from tests: 55 -> UrgentLow, 56 -> Low, 70 -> Low, 71 -> InRange, 179 -> InRange, 180 -> High, 249 -> High, 250 -> UrgentHigh.
Theme colors (constant across light/dark): InRange = Green500 0xFF22C55E, High = Low = Yellow500 0xFFEAB308, UrgentHigh = UrgentLow = Red500 0xFFEF4444. Low/High share one color and UrgentLow/UrgentHigh share one, so the color encodes SEVERITY not direction.
edge_cases: The color bands and the SQL Time-in-Range buckets do NOT use identical comparisons: color treats mgDl == low as Low and mgDl == high as High, while the TIR SQL counts [low, high] inclusive as in-range and (high, urgentHigh] as high, and glucose < urgentLow (not <=) as urgent-low. A value exactly at 'low' is colored Low but counted in-range.

capabilities.name: Trend arrow rendering
capabilities.behavior: trendArrowSymbol(CgmTrend) -> String, a pure function with no unit input. Mapping: DOUBLE_UP -> '⇈' (⇈), SINGLE_UP -> '↑' (↑), FORTY_FIVE_UP -> '↗' (↗), FLAT -> '→' (→), FORTY_FIVE_DOWN -> '↘' (↘), SINGLE_DOWN -> '↓' (↓), DOUBLE_DOWN -> '⇊' (⇊), UNKNOWN -> '?'. CgmTrend is persisted by enum NAME in Room; an unparseable stored name maps to CgmTrend.UNKNOWN on read. Spoken form for accessibility is the enum name lowercased with '_' replaced by ' ' (e.g. 'forty five up').
edge_cases: UNKNOWN renders a literal '?' in the same 40.sp bold hero style and the same severity color as the value.

capabilities.name: Glucose unit handling (mg/dL vs mmol/L) — GlucoseFormat
capabilities.behavior:
Storage, transport, every threshold comparison, alert detection, and the platform-wide 20–500 safety invariant all stay canonical mg/dL. GlucoseUnit only selects how a number is SHOWN and SPOKEN.

GlucoseUnit enum: MGDL(wireValue "mgdl"), MMOL(wireValue "mmol"). fromWire(String?) matches wireValue case-insensitively, unknown/null -> MGDL. fromName(String?) is valueOf() wrapped in try/catch, unknown/null/corrupt -> MGDL, never throws. Persisted in SharedPreferences as the enum NAME.

GlucoseFormat (pure Kotlin, no Android deps, so the watch surface can mirror it):
- MGDL_PER_MMOL = 18.0156 — the single canonical constant, mirroring backend src/core/units.py MGDL_PER_MMOL and the web MGDL_PER_MMOL. Explicit instruction in code: NEVER introduce a second value (18.02 / 18.0182); drift desyncs client from server.
- label(): 'mg/dL' / 'mmol/L'. spokenUnit(): 'milligrams per deciliter' / 'millimoles per liter'.
- convertValue(mgDl: Int, unit): MGDL -> value verbatim as Double; MMOL -> mgDl / 18.0156, UNROUNDED (round LAST at the display edge).
- convertSpread(mgDl: Double): offset-free divide-by-factor for standard deviations / differences. Deliberately distinct from convertValue: a spread has no zero anchor and keeps a decimal in mg/dL where a value is an integer. Reusing the value converter for a spread is called out in code as a bug.
- format(mgDl, unit): MGDL -> integer toString(); MMOL -> String.format(Locale.US, "%.1f", convertValue).
- formatWithLabel(): '<value> <label>' e.g. '120 mg/dL' / '6.7 mmol/L'.
- formatMean(Float, unit): MGDL -> "%.0f" (byte-identical to the legacy string); MMOL -> "%.1f" of the converted mean.
- formatSpread(Float, unit): one decimal in EITHER unit; mmol goes through convertSpread, never convertValue.
ALL formatting uses Locale.US so the decimal separator is always a dot — for cross-surface consistency and so mmol output still matches the release log scrubber.

Clinical anchors pinned by tests: 70 -> 3.9, 180 -> 10.0, 120 -> 6.7, 100 -> 5.6. Cross-surface fixture (must match web toFixed(1), watch GlucoseDisplayUtils, and API format_glucose_value): 54->3.0, 70->3.9, 99->5.5, 100->5.6, 120->6.7, 180->10.0, 250->13.9, 400->22.2. Bounds: 20 -> 1.1, 500 -> 27.8. A round-trip test bounds mmol display error at 0.05*18.0156 mg/dL.

HomeViewModel.glucoseUnit is a StateFlow seeded from the AppSettingsStore cache and fed by appSettingsStore.glucoseUnitFlow() (a SharedPreferences change-listener callbackFlow), so the dashboard re-renders the moment the unit changes in Settings or a backend reconcile writes the cache. The unit is a PER-ACCOUNT preference; init unconditionally calls authRepository.refreshGlucoseUnit() on every load (a cheap GET) — explicitly NOT gated on the glucose-range staleness clock, because that made a unit change on another device fail to propagate on a cold open while the range was still fresh.

What converts (display only): hero value, hero unit label, chart Y-axis labels, chart tooltip value, TIR bucket boundary labels and target caption, CGM-stats mean and std-dev. What NEVER converts: all thresholds/comparisons, chart geometry, TIR bucket counts (SQL, mg/dL), CV%, GMI (a % derived from the raw mg/dL mean), insulin units.
edge_cases: GAP IN TODAY'S BEHAVIOR: the Recent-Boluses / Bolus-History 'BG' column prints bolus.bgAtEvent?.toString() — the RAW mg/dL integer with no unit conversion and no unit label, even when the user's display unit is mmol/L. Every other glucose surface converts.
GlucoseUnit persists as enum NAME (MGDL/MMOL) locally but serializes as wireValue (mgdl/mmol) to the backend — two distinct string vocabularies.
Non-GlucoseFormat numeric strings on the dashboard (IoB, basal, battery, reservoir, CV%, GMI, TIR percentages) use the DEFAULT device locale, not Locale.US.

capabilities.name: Freshness / staleness classifier and per-source policy
capabilities.behavior:
Freshness enum: FRESH, STALE, TOO_STALE. Display policy per the doc comment: FRESH = render normally, age caption advisory only; STALE = show a 'last updated Xm ago' badge, value still shown; TOO_STALE = the value must NOT be presented as a current reading (for glucose this is a safety-grade de-emphasis).

FreshnessThresholds(staleAfterMs, tooStaleAfterMs) with an init require(staleAfterMs in 1 until tooStaleAfterMs) — construction throws IllegalArgumentException otherwise. classify(ageMs) uses HALF-OPEN boundaries: ageMs < staleAfterMs -> FRESH; ageMs < tooStaleAfterMs -> STALE; else TOO_STALE. A point exactly AT staleAfterMs is STALE, exactly AT tooStaleAfterMs is TOO_STALE. NEGATIVE ages (clock skew / future timestamp) classify as FRESH.

FreshnessPolicy (the documented display-safety decision, surfaced for PM/clinical sign-off):
- CGM = stale after 6 min (6 * 60_000 ms), too-stale after 15 min (15 * 60_000 ms). Rationale in code: sensors (Dexcom G6/G7, Libre) publish every ~5 min, so one missed reading (~6 min) is STALE but plausibly current; by ~15 min (three missed readings) trend and value can no longer be trusted as live.
- PUMP = stale after 15 min, too-stale after 60 min. Applies to IOB, basal, battery, reservoir (polled far less aggressively; not a safety-critical live vital).
- CGM_DEBUG_FAST = stale after 20_000 ms, too-stale after 45_000 ms. Debug-only, substituted ONLY when the debug 'Fast staleness' fault-injection toggle is on; never used in release paths (AppSettingsStore.debugFastStaleness is hard-gated on BuildConfig.DEBUG).
- cgm(debugFastStaleness: Boolean) is the single home for the swap rule so display, alert floor, and the degraded surface age CGM data identically.

relativeAgeLabel(ageMs) — pure, reusable by watch/complication surfaces: seconds = ageMs/1000; < 60 -> 'just now'; < 3600 -> '<n>m ago'; < 86_400 -> '<n>h ago'; else '<n>d ago'. Negative ages read as 'just now'. Pinned: 0 and 59_000 -> 'just now', 60_000 -> '1m ago', 59min -> '59m ago', 60min -> '1h ago', 23h -> '23h ago', 24h -> '1d ago'.

Explicit design decision recorded in code: the local freshness-gated alerting layer reuses this exact policy — do NOT fork a second staleness definition.
edge_cases: classify() deliberately calls negative ages FRESH (correct for display) — a separate, stricter predicate exists for alerting.
FreshnessThresholds construction with stale >= tooStale, or stale <= 0, throws rather than clamping.

capabilities.name: Freshness UI: ticking re-evaluation and staleness badge
capabilities.behavior:
rememberFreshness(timestamp: Instant, thresholds: FreshnessThresholds) -> FreshnessState(freshness, ageMs, label). Tick cadence = (thresholds.staleAfterMs / 4) coerced into [MIN_FRESHNESS_TICK_MS = 2_000L, FRESHNESS_TICK_MS = 30_000L]. So real CGM (6 min stale) ticks every 30 s (90 s / capped to 30 s); PUMP (15 min) also 30 s; CGM_DEBUG_FAST (20 s) ticks every 5 s. A LaunchedEffect keyed on (timestamp, thresholds) loops forever: delay(tickMs) then re-sample System.currentTimeMillis(). ageMs = now - timestamp.toEpochMilli(); the state is (classify(ageMs), ageMs, relativeAgeLabel(ageMs)). This makes the badge appear and the age grow WITHOUT any new reading arriving.

freshnessColor(): FRESH -> GlucoseColors.InRange (green), STALE -> GlucoseColors.High (amber/yellow), TOO_STALE -> colorScheme.onSurfaceVariant (grey).

StalenessBadge(freshness): returns/renders NOTHING when FRESH (so a fresh golden-path screen renders zero 'staleness_badge' nodes). STALE -> text 'Stale' in GlucoseColors.High; TOO_STALE -> text 'Too old' in onSurfaceVariant. Style labelSmall, background = same color at alpha 0.15 with RoundedCornerShape(4.dp), padding horizontal 6.dp / vertical 2.dp, testTag 'staleness_badge'.
edge_cases: The first tick happens AFTER the delay, so the initial render uses the composition-time clock.
Because the ticker restarts on a new timestamp, a fresh reading resets the cadence phase.

capabilities.name: Glucose trend chart — base rendering
capabilities.behavior:
Compose Canvas drawing (testTag 'glucose_chart'). Home mode wraps in a Card (surface color) with 16.dp inner padding and a fixed chart Box height of 280.dp; detail mode drops the Card and uses Modifier.weight(1f) to fill.

Geometry: leftPadding 36.dp, rightPadding 32.dp when there are IoB readings else 8.dp, topPadding 8.dp, bottomPadding 24.dp. Draw aborts early if xMax <= xMin (zero-span guard against divide-by-zero) or if chartWidth <= 0 or chartHeight <= 0.

Y axis is FIXED in mg/dL: CHART_Y_MIN = 40f, CHART_Y_MAX = 300f (yRange 260). Geometry always stays mg/dL; only the rendered label strings convert to the user's unit.

Draw order (back to front):
1. Target-range band: rect from y(high) to y(low) across the full chart width, GlucoseColors.InRange at alpha 0.08.
2. Grid lines at low, high, urgentHigh — dashed PathEffect(floatArrayOf(8f, 8f)), colorScheme.outline at alpha 0.3, strokeWidth 1f.
3. Y-axis labels at low, high, urgentHigh rendered with GlucoseFormat.format(value, unit), TextStyle(10.sp, onSurfaceVariant), right-aligned 3.dp left of the plot area, vertically centered on the line.
4. X-axis time labels. Format chosen by visibleHours = (xMax-xMin)/3_600_000: <= 6 -> 'h:mm'; <= 48 -> 'ha'; <= 168 -> 'EEE'; else 'M/d', in ZoneId.systemDefault(). tickCount by visibleHours: <=3 -> 3; <=6 -> 3; <=12 -> 4; <=24 -> 4; <=72 -> 3; <=168 -> 7; <=336 -> 7; else 6. Ticks are drawn for i in 0..tickCount inclusive (so tickCount+1 labels), evenly spaced, centered under their x, 4.dp below the plot area.
5. Mode overlay bands, 6. basal stepped area, 7. IoB overlay, 8. bolus markers (see separate capability).
9. Glucose dots LAST (on top): for each reading with xMin <= ts <= xMax, x = leftPadding + chartWidth*(ts-xMin)/(xMax-xMin); the value is CLAMPED to 40..300 for the y position but the COLOR uses the raw unclamped value via glucoseColor(); filled circle of radius 3.dp.

Empty state: when readings is empty, a centered 'No glucose readings yet' (bodyMedium, onSurfaceVariant) in a Box of height 280.dp (home) or weight(1f) (detail), testTag 'chart_empty_state'.

Header (home only, i.e. when onClick != null): a SpaceBetween Row with title 'Glucose Trend' (titleSmall) and a 48.dp IconButton with Icons.Default.OpenInFull, contentDescription 'Expand chart detail', testTag 'expand_chart_detail', then an 8.dp spacer.

Accessibility: the canvas carries contentDescription 'Glucose trend chart showing <n> readings over the last <period label>' plus ', with insulin on board overlay' / ', with basal rate overlay' / ', with <n> bolus markers' suffixes when those series are non-empty.

'now' is remembered keyed on (readings, iobReadings, basalReadings, bolusEvents, selectedPeriod, nowMsOverride) — sampled once per data change, not per frame; a nowMsOverride test seam pins it for deterministic renders.
edge_cases: Readings above 300 or below 40 mg/dL are pinned to the axis edge but keep their true severity color, so an out-of-axis extreme is visible as a colored dot on the boundary.
There is no line/spline between glucose points — only dots.
Y-axis labels are only at the three threshold values; there are no fixed 40/300 end labels.

capabilities.name: Chart overlays: basal, activity-mode bands, IoB, bolus markers, legend
capabilities.behavior:
Basal stepped area (drawBasalOverlay): skipped if empty. maxRate = max of all rates coerced into [0.1f, 15.0f]. Basal occupies the BOTTOM 25% of chart height (basalHeight = chartHeight * 0.25), anchored at the plot bottom. Each reading's segment runs from its timestamp to the next reading's timestamp (clamped to xMax) or to xMax for the last one; segments entirely outside the window are skipped; the start is clamped to xMin. segHeight = basalHeight * (rate / maxRate). Per-segment: a filled rect at alpha 0.15, a top edge line at alpha 0.6 with strokeWidth 1.5.dp, and (for i > 0, when the start is inside the window) a vertical step line from the previous segment's height at alpha 0.4, strokeWidth 1.dp. Segment color: SLEEP -> 0xFF7E57C2 purple; EXERCISE -> 0xFFFF9800 orange; else isAutomated -> 0xFF00BCD4 teal; else -> 0xFF78909C blue-grey.

Activity-mode overlay (drawModeOverlay): for basal readings whose activityMode is SLEEP or EXERCISE only, a FULL-HEIGHT background band across the segment's x-range at alpha 0.06 in the sleep-purple / exercise-orange color.

IoB overlay (drawIoBOverlay): requires at least 2 IoB readings (returns early otherwise). maxIob = max iob coerced to at least 1f. Points map to the FULL chart height on a secondary scale: y = topPadding + chartHeight * (1 - iob/maxIob). Builds a filled area path (down to the plot bottom at first and last in-window x) drawn at alpha 0.06 and a line path drawn at alpha 0.4 with strokeWidth 1.5.dp, both in colorScheme.primary. Right-hand Y-axis labels in TextStyle(9.sp, primary at alpha 0.6): the max value as "%.1fu" at the top, '0u' at the bottom, both 3.dp right of the plot area.

Bolus markers (drawBolusMarkers): skipped if empty. markerRadius 4.dp, minSpacing 20.dp, staggerStep 18.dp, baseMarkerY = topPadding + 16.dp, maxStaggerLevels = ((chartHeight * 0.25) / staggerStep) as Int, at least 1 (caps stagger so clustered boluses cannot overflow into the glucose area). Iterating in list order: if x - prevX < minSpacing the stagger level increments (capped), else it resets to 0; markerY = baseMarkerY + staggerLevel * staggerStep. Per marker: a dashed vertical line (PathEffect 4f/4f, alpha 0.3, strokeWidth 1.dp) from just below the marker down to the plot bottom; a filled DIAMOND path of markerRadius; a units label "%.1fu" (8.sp, marker color) centered above the marker, y clamped to >= 0; and, above that, a type tag (7.sp, marker color at alpha 0.8) whose y is also clamped to >= 0.
Marker color by DashboardComputations.deriveBolusType: AUTO_CORRECTION and AUTO -> BolusTypeColors.Correction (0xFFE91E63 pink); MEAL_WITH_CORRECTION -> 0xFFAB47BC medium purple; CORRECTION -> 0xFFFF5722 deep orange; MEAL -> 0xFF7C4DFF deep purple.
Type tag text (bolusTypeLabel): plain MEAL is deliberately SKIPPED (null) to reduce clutter. With no configured categoryLabels the fallbacks are 'Auto Corr' / 'Correction' / 'Meal+Corr' / 'Auto'. With labels configured they resolve from categoryLabels keys 'AUTO_CORRECTION', 'CORRECTION', 'FOOD_AND_CORRECTION'; BolusType.AUTO always uses the static 'Auto' because it has no dedicated BolusCategory and must not be conflated with AUTO_CORRECTION when users customize labels. All tags run through abbreviateLabel(): blank stays blank, <= 8 chars unchanged, otherwise first 7 chars + '.'.

Legend (ChartLegend): a centered Row with 8.dp spacing rendered below the plot (spacer 4.dp in detail mode, 6.dp on home). Entries appear only for series actually present in the data (computed with remember over basalReadings / bolusEvents): basal 'Auto'/'Manual'/'Sleep'/'Exercise' in their band colors, then bolus entries (auto-correction, auto, manual correction, meal+corr, meal) in their marker colors using the same categoryLabels + abbreviateLabel resolution, then 'IoB' in primary at alpha 0.7. Each entry is an 8.dp filled circle + 3.dp spacer + labelSmall text in the entry color.
edge_cases: A single IoB reading draws no overlay at all (and therefore also no right-hand axis labels), but the right padding still widens to 32.dp because that check is only iobReadings.isNotEmpty().
maxIob is floored at 1f so a tiny IoB does not fill the chart height.
Basal rates above 15 U/hr compress the whole basal scale (maxRate clamp).
The legend shows both 'Auto Corr' and 'Auto' entries in the SAME pink when both bolus types are present.

capabilities.name: Chart interaction: period chips, zoom, pan, tooltip (detail mode only)
capabilities.behavior:
Period selector: shown when showPeriodSelector is true — a centered Row of Material3 FilterChips, 4.dp horizontal padding each, RoundedCornerShape(8.dp), selected chip uses colorScheme.primary / onPrimary, testTag 'period_chip_<label>'. On the HOME card the chips are HOME_PERIODS = the first 4 ChartPeriod entries: 3H, 6H, 12H, 24H. ChartPeriod full enum (label, hours): THREE_HOURS('3H',3), SIX_HOURS('6H',6), TWELVE_HOURS('12H',12), TWENTY_FOUR_HOURS('24H',24), THREE_DAYS('3D',72), SEVEN_DAYS('7D',168), FOURTEEN_DAYS('14D',336), THIRTY_DAYS('30D',720). Default selected period is THREE_HOURS.

Gestures exist ONLY in detail mode (home mode attaches an empty Modifier):
- detectTransformGestures (keyed on selectedPeriod and nowMs): any gesture first dismisses the tooltip. Zoom: viewportSpan = (viewportSpan / zoom) coerced into [MIN_VISIBLE_MS = 15 * 60_000 (15 minutes), fullPeriodMs]. Pan: msPerPx = viewportSpan / canvasWidth; viewportCenter -= pan.x * msPerPx, then coerced into [fullStartMs + halfSpan, nowMs - halfSpan]. A canvas width of 0 aborts the pan.
- detectTapGestures: onDoubleTap resets viewportSpan = fullPeriodMs, viewportCenter = nowMs - fullPeriodMs/2, and clears the tooltip. onTap converts x to a timestamp via tapFraction = ((x - chartLeftPadding)/chartWidth) coerced 0..1, tapMs = drawXMin + tapFraction*(drawXMax-drawXMin); finds the nearest reading with a binary search over the timestamp-sorted list (checks the two candidates straddling the target); accepts it only if |nearest.ts - tapMs| < proximityMs where proximityMs = 3% of the visible span coerced into [60_000, 300_000] (1–5 minutes, scaling with zoom); otherwise clears the tooltip.
- Viewport: visibleStartMs = (center - span/2) coerced >= fullStartMs; visibleEndMs = (center + span/2) coerced <= nowMs. Home mode always draws the full [nowMs - fullPeriodMs, nowMs] window. viewportSpan/viewportCenter reset whenever selectedPeriod changes.

Tooltip (detail mode only): a Box offset to (readingX - 60.dp, readingY - 56.dp) clamped into the plot area (max x = chartLeftPadding+chartWidth-120.dp, max y = chartTopPadding+chartHeight-56.dp, both floored at 0), background colorScheme.surfaceVariant with RoundedCornerShape(8.dp), padding 10.dp/6.dp. Contents: GlucoseFormat.formatWithLabel(value, unit) in labelLarge colored by glucoseColor(), and the time formatted 'h:mm a' in the system zone (labelSmall, onSurfaceVariant).
edge_cases: Zooming can never show less than 15 minutes nor more than the selected period; you cannot pan past 'now' or before the period start.
The tooltip y is computed from the CLAMPED (40..300) glucose value, so a tooltip for an extreme reading anchors at the axis edge.
nowMs is frozen per data change, so a long-lived detail view's right edge does not advance until new data arrives.

capabilities.name: Chart / analytics data windows and period selection state
capabilities.behavior:
HomeViewModel owns five independent period selections, all exposed as StateFlows with matching on<X>PeriodSelected setters:
- selectedPeriod: ChartPeriod, default THREE_HOURS — drives cgmHistory, iobHistory, basalHistory, bolusHistory. Each is _selectedPeriod.flatMapLatest { since = Instant.ofEpochMilli(System.currentTimeMillis() - period.hours*3600_000) ; repository.observe<X>History(since) }.
- selectedTirPeriod: TirPeriod, default TWENTY_FOUR_HOURS — timeInRange combines the period with the live thresholds and calls repository.observeTimeInRange(since, urgentLow, low, high, urgentHigh) on a ROLLING now-minus-hours window.
- selectedCgmStatsPeriod: TirPeriod, default TWENTY_FOUR_HOURS — observeCgmHistoryAll(since) mapped through DashboardComputations.computeCgmStats(readings, period.hours), also a ROLLING window.
- selectedInsulinPeriod: TirPeriod, default TWENTY_FOUR_HOURS — combines period + dayBoundaryHour + activePumpPlugin; since = DashboardComputations.periodStart(period.daysBack, boundary, systemDefault zone), i.e. DAY-BOUNDARY-ALIGNED, then combines observeBasalHistoryAll + observeBolusHistoryAll into computeInsulinSummary(..., period.hours, categoryProvider).
- selectedBolusPeriod: TirPeriod, default TWENTY_FOUR_HOURS — same day-boundary-aligned since; combines bolus + CGM + IoB 'All' history into DashboardComputations.enrichBoluses.
TirPeriod(label, hours, daysBack): TWENTY_FOUR_HOURS('24H',24,0), THREE_DAYS('3D',72,2), SEVEN_DAYS('7D',168,6), FOURTEEN_DAYS('14D',336,13), THIRTY_DAYS('30D',720,29).

periodStart(daysBack, boundaryHour, zone, now): requires boundaryHour in 0..23; takes today's local date at boundaryHour; if now is before that boundary it rolls back one day; then subtracts daysBack days. This matches the pump's Delivery Summary which resets at midnight (boundary 0). dayBoundaryHour comes from AnalyticsSettingsStore (default 0), refreshed from GET /api/analytics config when stale (15 min) and coerced into 0..23.

All of these are stateIn(viewModelScope, SharingStarted.WhileSubscribed(5000), <seed>) — subscriptions (and therefore the recomputed 'since') are dropped 5 seconds after the last collector goes away.

Room query row caps: observe<X>History (the chart) LIMIT 2000 for CGM/IoB/basal and LIMIT 500 for bolus; observe<X>HistoryAll (the analytics cards) LIMIT 50000. All ordered timestampMs ASC; latest-value queries are ORDER BY timestampMs DESC LIMIT 1.
edge_cases: The 'since' instant is captured when the flow is (re)subscribed, NOT continuously — the window does not slide while the screen stays open; it re-anchors after the 5 s WhileSubscribed timeout expires and the screen is revisited.
TIR and CGM stats use rolling now-minus-N-hours windows while insulin summary and bolus lists use day-boundary-aligned windows — the same '24H' chip means different spans on different cards.
Chart history is capped at 2000 rows; a 30D chart with 5-minute CGM data (~8600 points) would be truncated at the oldest end for the chart series (the analytics 'All' variants are capped at 50000).

capabilities.name: Time in Range card
capabilities.behavior:
Card testTag 'tir_bar'. Header Row: title 'Time in Range' (titleSmall) and, only when data != null && totalReadings > 0, a quality label (labelMedium SemiBold, testTag 'tir_quality_label') from qualityAssessment(inRangePercent): >= 70 -> 'Excellent' green; >= 50 -> 'Good' yellow; else 'Needs Improvement' red.

Period chips: TirPeriod entries filtered by it.hours/24 <= max(maxRetentionDays, 1); the effective period falls back to the first available entry if the selection is filtered out (the card does NOT call back to change the VM selection — unlike CgmStatsCard). testTag 'tir_period_chip_<label>'.

Empty state (data == null or totalReadings == 0): centered 'No glucose readings for this period' (bodySmall, onSurfaceVariant).

With data: a 24.dp-tall five-bucket stacked bar clipped to RoundedCornerShape(12.dp) over a slate-700 (0xFF334155) background. Segments in order urgentLow / low / inRange / high / urgentHigh in the 5-bucket clinical palette (red / yellow / green / yellow / red). Each segment width = (pct/total)*totalWidth EXCEPT the last non-zero segment, which absorbs all rounding by taking the remaining width. Zero-percent buckets draw nothing; a total of <= 0 draws only the background.

Legend: two rows (3 entries then 2), SpaceEvenly, each an 8.dp circle + 4.dp spacer + '<bucket label>: <percent>' in the bucket color. Bucket labels (tirBucketLabels) are threshold boundaries rendered in the USER'S UNIT: '<urgentLow', 'urgentLow-low', 'low-high', 'high-urgentHigh', '>urgentHigh'. formatTirPercent: <= 0 -> '0%'; < 0.5 -> '<1%'; >= 99.5 and < 100 -> '>99%'; else '%.0f%%'.

Footer: tirTargetLabel = 'Target: <low>-<high> <unit label>' in the user's unit (testTag 'tir_target_range').

Accessibility: 'Time in range: %.0f%% urgent low, %.0f%% low, %.0f%% in range, %.0f%% high, %.0f%% urgent high, target <low>-<high> <spoken unit>, <n> readings over <period label>' or 'Time in range: no glucose readings for this period'.

The percentages themselves are SQL-computed in mg/dL by PumpDao.observeTimeInRangeCounts, which additionally filters glucoseMgDl BETWEEN 20 AND 500, with buckets: < urgentLow; >= urgentLow AND < low; >= low AND <= high; > high AND <= urgentHigh; > urgentHigh. TimeInRangeCounts -> TimeInRangeData converts counts to count*100f/total (all zeros when total == 0). TimeInRangeData's init requires every percent in 0..100, totalReadings >= 0, and the five percentages to sum to ~100 (within 0.5) unless they sum to < 0.5 (the all-zero case).
edge_cases: Because Low and High share Yellow500 and UrgentLow/UrgentHigh share Red500, the bar has visually identical colors on both ends — position, not hue, distinguishes low from high.
The TIR bucket for exactly 'low' or exactly 'high' is in-range, which differs from the hero color banding at those exact values.
TimeInRangeData's require() would throw on inconsistent percentages, so a malformed aggregate crashes rather than rendering.

capabilities.name: CGM Stats card and statistics computation
capabilities.behavior:
Card testTag 'cgm_stats_card', title 'CGM Stats'. Periods are restricted to 24H / 3D / 7D (CgmStatsPeriods), further filtered by it.hours/24 <= max(retentionDays,1); testTag 'cgm_stats_period_<label>'. Unlike the other cards, a LaunchedEffect actively calls onPeriodSelected(effectivePeriod) when the current selection is not available, pushing the correction back into the shared ViewModel state.

Empty state (stats == null): 'No glucose readings for this period'.

Two rows of three StatColumns (label / value / optional subtitle):
Row 1 — 'Mean Glucose' = GlucoseFormat.formatMean(mean, unit) + ' ' + unit label; 'Std Dev' = GlucoseFormat.formatSpread(stdDev, unit) with the unit label as subtitle; 'CV%' = '%.1f%%' colored and subtitled by cvAssessment: <= 36 -> 'Stable' green, <= 50 -> 'Moderate' yellow, else 'High' red.
Row 2 — 'GMI' = '%.1f%%' with subtitle 'est. A1C'; 'CGM Active' = '%.0f%%' colored and subtitled by cgmActiveAssessment: >= 70 -> 'Good' green, >= 50 -> 'Fair' yellow, else 'Low' red; 'Readings' = the raw count.

DashboardComputations.computeCgmStats(readings, periodHours):
- Filters to glucoseMgDl in 20..500 (VALID_GLUCOSE_MIN/MAX); returns null if nothing valid remains.
- mean = sum/size (Float).
- variance uses the SAMPLE denominator: (n-1) when n > 1, else 1; stdDev = sqrt(variance).
- cvPercent = (stdDev/mean)*100, or 0 when mean <= 0.
- gmi = 3.31 + 0.02392 * mean — computed from the RAW mg/dL mean and never unit-converted (explicitly pinned by a test).
- cgmActivePercent = valid.size * 100 / (periodHours * EXPECTED_READINGS_PER_HOUR=12), coerced into 0..100; when periodHours <= 0 it is 100.
Accessibility string: 'CGM statistics: mean glucose <v> <spoken unit>, std dev <v> <spoken unit>, CV %.1f%% <label>, GMI %.1f%%, CGM active %.0f%% <label>, <n> readings' or 'CGM statistics: no data available'.
edge_cases: The card and the ViewModel share ONE selectedCgmStatsPeriod with the insulin/bolus cards' own separate selections; the LaunchedEffect correction only fires for this card.
cgmActivePercent assumes exactly 12 readings/hour; a sensor with a different cadence misreports coverage.
Selecting 14D/30D is impossible on this card even at 30-day retention (CgmStatsPeriods is capped at 7D).

capabilities.name: Insulin summary card and computation (dosing display)
capabilities.behavior:
Card testTag 'insulin_summary_card', title 'Insulin Summary'. Periods restricted to 24H / 3D / 7D (InsulinPeriods) filtered by retention; testTag 'insulin_period_<label>'. Empty state: 'No insulin data for this period'.

Content: a large centered TDD value 'x.x U/day' (headlineMedium Bold, Locale.US); a 24.dp basal/bolus stacked bar (testTag 'insulin_stacked_bar', slate-700 background, basal 0xFF38BDF8 sky-400 then bolus 0xFF8B5CF6 violet-500, widths from the two percentages normalized by their sum, bolus absorbing the remainder; nothing drawn when the sum <= 0); a legend Row with 'Basal' and 'Bolus' each showing '%.1fU (%.0f%%)'; a divider; a portion block (testTag 'insulin_detail_stats') with two rows '<FOOD label> Bolus' and '<CORRECTION label> Bolus' each '%.1f U/d'; then, when categoryBreakdown is non-empty, a divider, a '<n> boluses' header, and a per-category list (testTag 'insulin_category_breakdown') in the fixed CATEGORY_DISPLAY_ORDER FOOD_AND_CORRECTION, CORRECTION, FOOD, AUTO_CORRECTION, OVERRIDE, AI_SUGGESTED, OTHER — each row an 8.dp color dot (colorForCategory), the label, the count (width 28.dp, right-aligned), and the share '%3.0f%%' (width 36.dp). When the debug 'Show Pump Labels' toggle is on, the label becomes '<display label> (<pump-native label>)' using the reverse map built from the active plugin's BolusCategoryProvider. When categoryBreakdown IS empty, a fallback footer '<n> boluses (<m> corrections)'.

DashboardComputations.computeInsulinSummary(basals, boluses, periodHours, categoryProvider):
- Returns null when periodHours <= 0, or when totalBasal + totalBolus <= 0.
- totalBolus = sum of bolus units. totalBasal = computeBasalIntegral: each basal segment runs from its timestamp to the next reading's timestamp, or to System.currentTimeMillis() for the last one, with the segment duration CAPPED at 2.0 hours (and floored at 0) to avoid inflated gaps; units += rate * cappedHours.
- Denominator: days = (dataSpanHours / 24) coerced into [1f, periodHours/24f], where dataSpanHours = (now - oldest event timestamp)/3_600_000. Explicitly uses now (not the newest event) so the denominator matches computeBasalIntegral's numerator, and the 1-day floor prevents sub-day data inflating into huge daily projections.
- correctionBoluses = boluses where isCorrection || correctionUnits > 0; totalCorrection sums correctionUnits when > 0 else the full units.
- Portion accumulation per bolus (mutually exclusive branches): isAutomated -> the whole thing is correction (correctionUnits if > 0 else units) because automated boluses have no meal component; else if mealUnits > 0 || correctionUnits > 0 -> use the declared portions directly; else if isCorrection -> full units to correction; else -> full units to food.
- Category assignment per bolus via BolusCategoryMapper.resolve: use the plugin's BolusCategoryProvider.toPlatformCategory(bolus.category) when a provider exists AND bolus.category is non-empty (unknown platform names fall back to BolusCategory.OTHER); otherwise deriveFromFlags: isAutomated -> AUTO_CORRECTION; mealUnits > 0 && correctionUnits > 0 -> FOOD_AND_CORRECTION; isCorrection -> CORRECTION; mealUnits > 0 -> FOOD; else FOOD (manual bolus default).
- Outputs (all per-day): totalDailyDose = (basal+bolus)/days, basalUnits, bolusUnits, correctionUnits, foodBolusUnits, correctionBolusUnits; basalPercent = basalPerDay/tdd*100 (0 when tdd <= 0), bolusPercent = 100 - basalPercent (0 when tdd <= 0); bolusCount = boluses.size; correctionCount = correctionBoluses.size; categoryBreakdown of CategoryStats(count, totalUnits, foodPortion, correctionPortion); periodDays = days.
BolusCategory display names: AUTO_CORRECTION 'Auto Corr', FOOD 'Meal', FOOD_AND_CORRECTION 'Meal+Corr', CORRECTION 'Correction', OVERRIDE 'Override', AI_SUGGESTED 'AI Suggested', OTHER 'Other'. colorForCategory: AUTO_CORRECTION pink, FOOD deep purple, FOOD_AND_CORRECTION medium purple, CORRECTION deep orange, OVERRIDE 0xFFFFA000 amber, AI_SUGGESTED 0xFF00BCD4 cyan, OTHER blue-grey.
Accessibility: 'Insulin summary: total daily dose %.1f units, basal %.1f units (%.0f%%), bolus %.1f units (%.0f%%). <FOOD> bolus %.1f, <CORRECTION> bolus %.1f units per day. %d total boluses' (Locale.US) or 'Insulin summary: no data available'.
edge_cases: The basal integral uses the WALL CLOCK (System.currentTimeMillis()) inside a pure-looking compute function, so the same inputs give different results over time.
A 2-hour cap per basal segment means a long pump disconnect silently under-reports basal rather than extrapolating.
With a 24H period the days denominator is always exactly 1 (coerceIn(1, 1)), so TDD equals the raw total.

correctionUnits/mealUnits are the REQUESTED breakdown and may not sum to the DELIVERED units (partial delivery, status-response opcode 0x30 with no breakdown, automated boluses with mealUnits=0) — documented on BolusEvent.
Categories not present in the data are simply absent from the ordered list; unknown plugin category names collapse to OTHER.

capabilities.name: Recent boluses card and Bolus History screen
capabilities.behavior:
RecentBolusesCard (testTag 'recent_boluses_card'), title 'Recent Boluses' with an optional 48.dp expand IconButton (OpenInFull, contentDescription 'View all boluses', testTag 'expand_bolus_detail'). Periods 24H / 3D / 7D filtered by retention (testTag 'bolus_period_<label>'). Empty state 'No boluses for this period'.

Table header (shared with the detail screen): columns Time (weight 1.2), Units (0.8), Type (1.2), BG (0.8), IoB (0.8), all labelSmall SemiBold onSurfaceVariant.
Rows: sorted by timestamp DESCENDING, capped at MAX_HOME_ROWS = 5 on the card; separated by thin dividers. Each row is a Column of: a Row with the timestamp formatted 'M/d h:mm a' in the system zone; units '%.2fU' (Locale.US) SemiBold; a BolusTypeBadge; the BG value as the raw Int toString() or '--'; the IoB as '%.1fU' or '--'. Below the row, the derived reason string in labelSmall onSurfaceVariant.
BolusTypeBadge: white labelSmall SemiBold text on the type color at alpha 0.85, RoundedCornerShape(4.dp), padding 6.dp/1.dp, maxLines 1 with ellipsis. Labels resolve from categoryLabels keys AUTO_CORRECTION / CORRECTION / FOOD / FOOD_AND_CORRECTION with fallbacks 'Auto Corr' / 'Correction' / 'Meal' / 'Meal+Corr'; BolusType.AUTO always uses the static 'Auto'.
When boluses.size > 5 and onExpand exists, a full-width TextButton 'View all <n> boluses' (testTag 'view_all_boluses').
Card a11y: 'Recent boluses: <n> events in the last <period label>'.

BolusHistoryScreen: a DetailScaffold titled 'Bolus History' with a back arrow, BackHandler wired to onBack, sharing the HOME NavBackStackEntry's HomeViewModel (so the period selection is the same state). Period chips here use the FULL TirPeriod entry list filtered by retentionDays (note: unlike the cards, no coerceAtLeast(1) on retention), testTag 'bolus_history_period_<label>'. Empty state 'No boluses for this period'. Otherwise the same header + a LazyColumn (testTag 'bolus_history_list') of all boluses sorted descending, each followed by a divider.

Enrichment (DashboardComputations.enrichBoluses): returns empty for no boluses. CGM and IoB lists are defensively re-sorted ascending only if not already sorted. For each bolus, a binary search finds the nearest CGM and nearest IoB reading; the match is accepted only when |delta| <= CROSS_REF_WINDOW_MS = 5 * 60_000 (±5 minutes), otherwise null. bolusType = deriveBolusType: isAutomated && isCorrection -> AUTO_CORRECTION; mealUnits > 0 && correctionUnits > 0 -> MEAL_WITH_CORRECTION; isCorrection && !isAutomated -> CORRECTION; isAutomated -> AUTO; else MEAL. reason = deriveBolusReason: AUTO_CORRECTION 'Auto correction bolus'; CORRECTION 'BG correction bolus'; MEAL 'Food bolus'; MEAL_WITH_CORRECTION 'Meal %.1fU + correction %.1fU' (Locale.US) when both portions are > 0 else 'Meal bolus with correction'; AUTO 'Automated bolus'. A test pins that reasons contain no vendor-specific branding. EnrichedBolusEvent's init re-validates units/correctionUnits/mealUnits in 0..25 U and bgAtEvent in 20..500 mg/dL.
edge_cases: The BG column shows a bare mg/dL integer with NO unit conversion and NO unit label — the one glucose surface that ignores the user's mmol/L preference.
Boluses at the exact same timestamp both cross-reference to the same nearest CGM/IoB.
A bolus with no CGM/IoB within ±5 min shows '--'.
BolusHistoryScreen's period filter uses raw retentionDays without the >=1 floor used elsewhere, so a 0-day retention setting would yield an empty chip list.

capabilities.name: Dashboard data flows, settings reconciliation, and manual refresh
capabilities.behavior:
HomeViewModel exposes StateFlows: connectionState (from PumpDriver.observeConnectionState, seed DISCONNECTED), networkStatus (NetworkMonitor.status directly), cgmFreshnessThresholds (debugFastStalenessFlow mapped to CGM_DEBUG_FAST/CGM, seed CGM), cgm / iob / basalRate / battery / reservoir (latest-row Room flows, seed null), syncStatus (BackendSyncManager.syncStatus), backendConfigured (AuthTokenStore.backendConfiguredFlow, seed false), activePluginIds (sorted), pluginCards (flatMapLatest over all active plugins' observeDashboardCards, flattened and sorted by priority), glucoseThresholds, dayBoundaryHour, categoryLabels, pumpLabelMap, showPumpLabels, dataRetentionDays, glucoseUnit, isRefreshing. Almost all use SharingStarted.WhileSubscribed(5000).

init-time reconciliation (each in its own coroutine, failures logged and swallowed):
- authRepository.refreshGlucoseUnit() — UNCONDITIONAL every load.
- authRepository.refreshMealIntelligence() — UNCONDITIONAL every load.
- refreshGlucoseRange() if glucoseRangeStore.isStale(RANGE_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS = 900_000 ms / 15 min).
- refreshSafetyLimits() + pluginRegistry.refreshSafetyLimits() if safetyLimitsStore.isStale() (1 hour).
- refreshAlertThresholds() on Dispatchers.IO, ONLY when authRepository.isBackendConfigured() && alertThresholdStore.isStale() (1 hour) — skipped in BLE-only mode because LOCAL thresholds have no fetch timestamp so isStale() would be permanently true; the mode check runs on IO so the encrypted store read cannot block main-thread init.
- refreshAnalyticsConfig() if analyticsSettingsStore.isStale() (15 min).
- refreshPumpProfile() if pumpProfileStore.isStale() (1 hour).
- A collector on pluginRegistry.activePumpPlugin (distinctUntilChangedBy id) that PUT/DELETEs plugin category declarations to the backend.

refreshData() (pull-to-refresh): guarded by _isRefreshing.compareAndSet(false, true) so concurrent refreshes are dropped. Launches the settings refreshes concurrently (glucose range, glucose unit, meal intelligence, analytics config, pump profile, safety limits + plugin limits, alert thresholds), then performs BLE reads SEQUENTIALLY with delay(PumpPollingOrchestrator.REQUEST_STAGGER_MS = 500 ms) between them, in this order: getIoB, getBasalRate, getBatteryStatus, getReservoirLevel, getCgmStatus. Each success writes to the repository. The CGM result additionally goes through pollingOrchestrator.processCgmReading(it) so a low fetched by a manual refresh during an outage reaches the alert floor (and the watch relay) immediately rather than waiting for the next background poll. Finally the non-reactive settings dataRetentionDays and showPumpLabels are re-read. isRefreshing is reset in a finally block.

Background poll cadence (context for freshness): PumpPollingOrchestrator INTERVAL_FAST_MS = 15_000 (IoB + basal + CGM, also a keep-alive because the pump drops idle connections at ~30 s), INTERVAL_MEDIUM_MS = 300_000 (bolus history), INTERVAL_SLOW_MS = 300_000 (battery + reservoir), REQUEST_STAGGER_MS = 500, INITIAL_POLL_DELAY_MS = 500.
edge_cases: dataRetentionDays and showPumpLabels are snapshots, not reactive — they only update on refreshData() or a new ViewModel.
All refresh failures are logged at warn and leave the previous cached values intact (refreshSafetyLimits explicitly falls back to last-known-good).
pumpLabelMap construction is wrapped in try/catch around the plugin call and yields null on any failure or empty declaration set.

capabilities.name: Glucose threshold sourcing and validation
capabilities.behavior:
Thresholds come from GlucoseRangeStore (SharedPreferences 'glucose_range', defaults urgentLow 55 / low 70 / high 180 / urgentHigh 250, STALE_THRESHOLD_MS 3_600_000 = 1 hour, updateAll writes all four plus the fetch timestamp in ONE transaction so a kill mid-write cannot leave inconsistent state). HomeViewModel seeds _glucoseThresholds from the store and refreshes from GET glucose-range when stale by more than 15 minutes.

refreshGlucoseRange() validation on the backend response, in order: each of urgentLow / lowTarget / highTarget / urgentHigh is coerced into [MIN_THRESHOLD = 20, MAX_THRESHOLD = 500]; then an ordering check — if urgentLow > low || low >= high || high > urgentHigh, the whole update is REJECTED (logged at warn, previous thresholds preserved). Only a valid, ordered set is written to the store, and the StateFlow is updated only when the value actually changes. A non-2xx response or exception logs and leaves the cache untouched.

Thresholds feed: glucoseColor bands, the chart's target band + grid lines + Y-axis labels, the TIR SQL bucket boundaries and legend/target labels. Changing them re-triggers the TIR flow (timeInRange combines the period with _glucoseThresholds).
edge_cases: low == high is rejected (low >= high), but urgentLow == low and high == urgentHigh are allowed.
Thresholds are always mg/dL on the wire and in storage regardless of the user's display unit.

capabilities.name: Navigation structure
capabilities.behavior:
Screen sealed class (route, label, icon): Home 'home', AiChat 'ai_chat', Alerts 'alerts', Settings 'settings', Pairing 'pairing', BleDebug 'ble_debug', Onboarding 'onboarding', PluginDetail 'plugin_detail/{pluginId}/{cardId}', ChartDetail 'chart_detail', TirDetail 'tir_detail', InsulinDetail 'insulin_detail', AlertHistory 'alert_history', BolusHistory 'bolus_history', MealLog 'meal_log', MealHistory 'meal_history', CommonFoods 'common_foods', Licenses 'licenses'.

Bottom nav is CAPABILITY-DRIVEN, not static: bottomNavItems(backendConfigured) = [Home] + (AiChat only when backendConfigured) + [Alerts, Settings]. AI Chat is backend-only (there is no on-device model), so in BLE-only mode the tab is absent rather than dead-ending on a 'check your server URL' error. Tab clicks navigate with popUpTo(startDestination){saveState=true}, launchSingleTop, restoreState. Selection uses destination hierarchy matching.

spokeRoutes (own TopAppBar + back button; bottom nav HIDDEN): ChartDetail, TirDetail, InsulinDetail, AlertHistory, BolusHistory, PluginDetail, Pairing, BleDebug, MealLog, MealHistory, CommonFoods, Licenses. Bottom nav is also hidden on Onboarding.

startDestinationRoute(onboardingComplete) = Home if complete else Onboarding — keyed on onboarding completion ALONE, deliberately independent of session validity, because routing an expired session to Onboarding would lock local Room-served pump/CGM reads behind a login that cannot succeed offline. A session-less Home shows the tappable session banner instead, and every network surface keeps its own guard. The start destination is remembered once (not reactive).

sessionBannerMessage(state, backendConfigured): Expired -> its message unconditionally (it can only be reached from a session that once existed, and the nudge must survive an unreadable base URL); Unauthenticated -> 'Not signed in, tap to sign in' ONLY when backendConfigured (a BLE-only user is permanently Unauthenticated by design); Initializing / Refreshing / Authenticated -> null (Initializing is the pre-validation default and rendering a banner off it would flash 'not signed in' at cold start). The banner is an errorContainer-colored clickable Row with a Warning icon (decorative, contentDescription null) that navigates to Settings; hidden during onboarding.

backendGatedComposable(route, ...) wraps AiChat, MealLog, MealHistory, CommonFoods: the composable stays REGISTERED in BLE-only mode (dropping it would blank a restored back stack or deep link) but the body redirects to Home via navigate(Home){popUpTo(startDestination){saveState=true}; launchSingleTop} so neither back navigation nor state restoration can land on the empty guard frame. The mode is passed as rememberUpdatedState(...) because the NavHost builder's content lambdas are long-lived closures — a by-value capture would freeze the gating decision at graph-build time and ignore a server added or removed mid-session.

ChartDetail and BolusHistory resolve the HOME back-stack entry and share its HomeViewModel via hiltViewModel(homeEntry); if that entry is missing (IllegalArgumentException) they pop back immediately.

Other navigation effects: a logout event from SettingsViewModel navigates to Onboarding with popUpTo(0){inclusive=true}; when authState becomes Authenticated while on Onboarding AND onboardingComplete, it navigates to Home popping Onboarding. BleDebug is only registered when BuildConfig.DEBUG. PluginDetail takes two String nav args, URI-encoded at the call site. A PlaceholderScreen composable (centered headlineMedium title) exists for stubs.
edge_cases: backendConfigured is derived from the SAME reactive baseUrl collection whose initial value is a synchronous read — deliberately NOT from a pessimistic false seed, which would yank a restored AI-chat back stack to Home on the first frame for a full-stack user.
TirDetail, InsulinDetail and AlertHistory are registered routes but only render placeholder text today.
Onboarding hides both the bottom nav and the session banner but NOT the insecure-HTTP banner.

capabilities.name: Detail screens
capabilities.behavior:
DetailScaffold(title, onBack, content): a Material3 Scaffold with a TopAppBar showing the title and a back IconButton (ArrowBack, contentDescription 'Back'); testTag 'detail_scaffold_<title lowercased, spaces->underscores>'.

ChartDetailScreen: does NOT use DetailScaffold. A DisposableEffect forces the Activity's requestedOrientation to SCREEN_ORIENTATION_SENSOR_LANDSCAPE on enter and restores the original (or SCREEN_ORIENTATION_UNSPECIFIED) on dispose; if the context is not an Activity it logs a warning and skips the lock. capabilities.name: Alert-floor freshness gate (defined in this subsystem, consumed by alerting)
capabilities.behavior:
isFreshForAlertFloor(ageMs, thresholds) is the GLY-115 gate: true only when a reading of that age (now MINUS the CGM's own sensor timestamp, never poll wall-clock) may drive an on-device alarm or a 'this phone is watching' claim. It requires ageMs >= -ALERT_FLOOR_MAX_FUTURE_SKEW_MS (60_000 ms) AND thresholds.classify(max(ageMs, 0)) == FRESH. STALE and TOO_STALE both FAIL — the alarm is suppressed and the surface flips to an honest 'not watching'. The skew guard exists because classify() calls negative ages FRESH (correct for display) but a forward-skewed sensor timestamp must not pass as fresh; conversely a hard age >= 0 would silently disable the floor for any user whose pump clock runs slightly ahead.
Documented residual risk: this stateless predicate cannot see a BACKWARD wall-clock jump (which shrinks ageMs and makes a stale reading look fresh). That direction is guarded statefully by AlertFloor's wall-clock high-water mark (isWallClockRewound, mirrored by AlertFloorStatusProvider) which suppresses evaluation while 'now' runs behind previously observed time. Accepted residual: a rewind larger than the tolerance while the process is not running leaves no water mark and can under-age a stale reading — a rare over-alarm edge that fails toward alarming, never toward silence; rewinds within tolerance can under-age by at most 60_000 ms.
AlertFloorStatusProvider mirrors FreshnessUi's cadence discipline: tick = staleAfterMs/4 coerced into [2_000, 30_000] ms, so the 'watching' claim decays on its own with no new readings; the pipeline retries on failure after 5_000 ms, emitting a pessimistic snapshot first ('the claim degrades, it never lies or stops'), and the synchronous current() seed deliberately passes cgmAgeMs = null and backendConfigured = false so a safety surface can under-claim but never over-claim.
edge_cases: The gate uses the sensor's own timestamp, never the poll time — porting this with a receive timestamp would silently break the guarantee.
The debug fast-staleness policy also applies to the alert floor (FreshnessPolicy.cgm(debugFastStaleness)), so the debug toggle changes alarm behavior in debug builds.

capabilities.name: Domain model validation and persistence mapping
capabilities.behavior:
CgmReading requires glucoseMgDl in MIN_MG_DL=20..MAX_MG_DL=500 (the physiologically valid CGM bounds, shared with ingestion-side validation) or the constructor throws. BolusEvent requires units, correctionUnits and mealUnits all >= 0 and <= MAX_BOLUS_UNITS = 25f (hard safety cap; Tandem hardware max is 25 U). EnrichedBolusEvent re-validates the same 0..25 U bounds plus bgAtEvent in 20..500. TimeInRangeData validates every percent in 0..100, totalReadings >= 0, and the sum ~100 (±0.5) unless all-zero. FreshnessThresholds validates ordering. DashboardComputations.periodStart requires boundaryHour in 0..23. AnalyticsSettingsStore.updateAll requires dayBoundaryHour in 0..23.

Room -> domain mapping is FAIL-SAFE by dropping: CgmReadingEntity.toDomain() returns null (row silently skipped) when the stored glucose is out of the current 20..500 bounds — 'legacy data may have out-of-range glucose values (pre-validation)'; BolusEventEntity.toDomain() likewise returns null for rows violating current safety bounds. Unknown CgmTrend names map to UNKNOWN; unknown/legacy PumpActivityMode names (e.g. 'STANDARD') map to NONE. Room schema: cgm_readings and basal_readings have UNIQUE indices on timestampMs; bolus_events has a UNIQUE index on (units, timestampMs); CGM/basal batch inserts use OnConflictStrategy.IGNORE while single inserts use REPLACE. Retention cleanup (deleteAllBefore) runs transactionally across all six tables; PumpDataRepository.DEFAULT_RETENTION_MS = 7 days, and AppSettingsStore.dataRetentionDays defaults to 7 and is coerced into 1..30 on write.
edge_cases: A reading outside 20..500 is invisible to the dashboard entirely (dropped at the mapper), not shown as an error — the hero would fall back to the next-newest valid reading or '--'.
The bolus UNIQUE index on (units, timestampMs) means two genuinely distinct boluses with identical units at the identical millisecond collapse to one row.

capabilities.name: Shared presentation utilities (insecure-HTTP indicator, markdown sanitization)
capabilities.behavior: InsecureHttpBanner: a full-width errorContainer Row with a NoEncryption icon and the text 'Insecure LAN HTTP is on -- traffic to your server is unencrypted.' (bodySmall, onErrorContainer), padding 16.dp/8.dp, testTag 'insecure_http_banner'. Rendered at the very top of the NavHost content ABOVE everything including onboarding, whenever UrlSecurityPolicy.isActiveInsecureHttp(baseUrl, BuildConfig.DEBUG, allowInsecureLanHttp) is true — both halves observed reactively (settings flow + base-URL flow) so it tracks a toggle flip OR a server-URL change immediately. InsecureHttpConfirmDialog is the shared 'I understand the risk' acknowledgement (Warning icon in error tint, title 'Allow insecure LAN HTTP?', the shared INSECURE_HTTP_RISK_TEXT body, 'Enable' in error color with testTag 'insecure_http_confirm', 'Cancel'). AppMarkdownText: renders markdown with this app's link policy — image markdown and HTML tags are STRIPPED via three regexes before rendering, to prevent outbound image fetches from AI-generated content (mirrors the web MarkdownContent image suppression), and onLinkClicked only opens URLs whose lowercase form starts with 'https://' or 'http://' (ActivityNotFoundException and SecurityException are caught and logged). Blank markdown renders nothing. linkifyMask defaults to EMAIL_ADDRESSES|PHONE_NUMBERS|WEB_URLS; callers rendering prose containing file names should pass 0 because WEB_URLS reads 'some-file.md' as a domain.
edge_cases: The insecure-HTTP banner is derived from the policy (single source of truth) so it never shows for a public http:// URL the request layer would reject outright.

safety_critical: Glucose validity bounds are 20–500 mg/dL and are enforced in FOUR independent places that must all be ported: CgmReading's constructor (MIN_MG_DL=20 / MAX_MG_DL=500, throws), DashboardComputations VALID_GLUCOSE_MIN/MAX (filters CGM stats input), the TIR SQL 'glucoseMgDl BETWEEN 20 AND 500' filter, and HomeViewModel's threshold coercion MIN_THRESHOLD=20 / MAX_THRESHOLD=500. EnrichedBolusEvent additionally requires bgAtEvent in 20..500. Room rows outside these bounds are silently DROPPED at the entity->domain mapper (returns null), so an out-of-range value never renders at all.

Unit conversion has exactly ONE constant, GlucoseFormat.MGDL_PER_MMOL = 18.0156, mirroring the backend src/core/units.py MGDL_PER_MMOL and the web constant. The code carries an explicit instruction never to introduce a second value (18.02 / 18.0182) because drift desyncs client from server. The rule is convert ONCE from the most precise mg/dL source and round LAST (one decimal for mmol). Clinical anchors that must hold: 70->3.9, 180->10.0, 120->6.7, 100->5.6; cross-surface fixture 54->3.0, 99->5.5, 250->13.9, 400->22.2; bounds 20->1.1, 500->27.8. Locale.US is forced everywhere in GlucoseFormat so the separator is always a dot.

Spread conversion is a DISTINCT function: convertSpread / formatSpread divide by the factor with no zero-anchor and always render one decimal. Reusing the value converter for a standard deviation is called out in the code as a bug.
GMI is computed as 3.31 + 0.02392 * mean from the RAW mg/dL mean and must NEVER be unit-converted (a dedicated unit test pins this). CV% likewise stays a percentage of raw mg/dL.

Staleness policy is a documented display-safety decision requiring PM/clinical sign-off: CGM STALE at 6 min, TOO_STALE at 15 min; PUMP STALE at 15 min, TOO_STALE at 60 min; half-open boundaries (exactly at a threshold crosses into the worse state). At TOO_STALE the glucose value LOSES its severity color and renders grey, gains a 'Too old' badge, and the accessibility description says 'reading is stale, last updated X' BEFORE reading out any other metric — a stale number must never be presented as a live one.

The freshness UI re-evaluates on a ticker (staleAfterMs/4 clamped to 2–30 s) so the staleness badge appears and the age grows WITHOUT any new reading arriving. A port that only recomputes on data arrival would leave a dead sensor displaying a confident, green, hours-old number forever.

The alert-floor freshness gate isFreshForAlertFloor requires STRICTLY FRESH plus ageMs >= -60_000 ms (ALERT_FLOOR_MAX_FUTURE_SKEW_MS), computed against the CGM's OWN SENSOR TIMESTAMP, never the poll/receive wall-clock. STALE and TOO_STALE both suppress the alarm and flip the surface to an honest 'not watching'. Backward wall-clock jumps are guarded statefully by AlertFloor's high-water mark; the documented accepted residual fails toward alarming, never toward silence.

Insulin/dosing display: BolusEvent enforces a hard cap of MAX_BOLUS_UNITS = 25f on units, correctionUnits and mealUnits (Tandem hardware max), re-validated on EnrichedBolusEvent. Rows violating the cap are dropped rather than displayed. correctionUnits/mealUnits are the REQUESTED breakdown and may legitimately not sum to the DELIVERED units (partial delivery, occlusion, user cancel, status opcode 0x30 with no breakdown, automated boluses with mealUnits=0) — displaying them as if they summed would misrepresent delivered insulin.

The basal integral caps each segment at 2.0 hours and extends the final segment to System.currentTimeMillis(); the TDD denominator uses now (not the newest event) and is floored at 1 day. These choices deliberately under-report rather than extrapolate across gaps — a port that changes either half desyncs numerator and denominator and misstates total daily dose.

Glucose threshold updates from the backend are rejected wholesale when the ordering invariant fails (urgentLow > low || low >= high || high > urgentHigh), after each value is coerced into 20..500. A rejected update leaves the previous cached thresholds intact rather than applying a partially-valid range that would mis-band and mis-bucket readings.

UNIT-HANDLING GAP IN CURRENT BEHAVIOR: the Recent-Boluses and Bolus-History 'BG' column prints the raw mg/dL integer with no conversion and no unit label. An mmol/L user reading '65' in that column is being shown mg/dL. Every other glucose surface converts. Decide explicitly whether the Swift port replicates or fixes this.

Locale inconsistency: GlucoseFormat forces Locale.US, but the hero's IoB / basal / battery / reservoir values and their accessibility strings, the TIR percentages, and the CGM-stats CV%/GMI/active% use Kotlin's default-locale String.format. On a comma-decimal device the dashboard mixes '6.7 mmol/L' with '1,23u' for insulin on board.

map.notes:
Everything above was read from source; nothing is inferred from naming.

Cross-cutting facts a Swift engineer will need that don't fit one capability:

1. Single-ViewModel dashboard. One HomeViewModel instance backs Home, ChartDetail and BolusHistory (the detail screens resolve the Home NavBackStackEntry and reuse its ViewModel). Period selections, thresholds and unit are therefore shared state across those three screens, and every StateFlow uses SharingStarted.WhileSubscribed(5000) — leaving a screen for more than 5 seconds tears down the Room subscriptions and re-anchors every 'since' timestamp on return. This 5-second grace window is load-bearing for rotation/navigation.

2. mg/dL is canonical everywhere. Storage, transport, thresholds, alerting, chart geometry, TIR SQL buckets, GMI and CV all operate on mg/dL Ints. Only a small, enumerable set of rendered strings converts (hero value, hero/label captions, chart Y-axis labels, chart tooltip, TIR bucket + target labels, CGM-stats mean/std-dev). The one exception that is arguably a bug is the bolus table's BG column (flagged in safety_critical).

3. Explicit "we deliberately did NOT do X" decisions found in code comments, all load-bearing:
   - No backend health endpoint: reachability is derived purely from traffic the app already makes, flipping to unreachable only after FAILURE_THRESHOLD = 2 consecutive TRANSPORT failures (any HTTP status, even 4xx/5xx, proves reachability). Device-offline takes precedence over backend-unreachable.
   - NET_CAPABILITY_VALIDATED is deliberately NOT required — a LAN-only network with a self-hosted backend still counts as online.
   - The healthy sync icon is SwapVert (up/down arrows), deliberately not a cloud, so it cannot be confused with the healthy reachability cloud-check.
   - The start destination is keyed on onboarding completion ALONE and deliberately independent of session validity, so an expired session cannot lock local Room-served readings behind an impossible offline login.
   - The session banner deliberately stays silent while AuthState.Initializing to avoid a cold-start "not signed in" flash, and stays silent for Unauthenticated in BLE-only mode.
   - Backend-only routes stay REGISTERED in BLE-only mode and redirect, rather than being dropped from the graph, so restored back stacks and deep links do not blank.
   - The glucose-unit and meal-intelligence reconciles are deliberately NOT gated on the glucose-range staleness clock (a prior bug: a unit change on another device would not propagate on a cold open).
   - Plain MEAL bolus tags are deliberately omitted from chart markers to reduce clutter; BolusType.AUTO deliberately always uses the static label "Auto" so custom labels cannot conflate it with AUTO_CORRECTION.
   - Manufacturer brand marks were an explicit project-lead decision (nominative use).
   - MealConfidenceColors Medium and Low intentionally share one amber hue, distinguished by bar length not color alone; the safety qualifier strip is deliberately amber and never the red error color.
   - freshness classify() deliberately treats negative ages as FRESH for display, with a separate stricter predicate for alerting.

4. Numbers inventory (single list for the port): freshness CGM 6 min / 15 min, PUMP 15 min / 60 min, debug-fast 20 s / 45 s, alert-floor future-skew tolerance 60 s, freshness tick staleAfterMs/4 clamped [2 s, 30 s]; relative-age label breakpoints 60 s / 3600 s / 86400 s. Chart: Y axis 40–300 mg/dL, height 280 dp on home, paddings 36/8-or-32/8/24 dp, dot radius 3 dp, basal band 25% of height with rate clamp 0.1–15 U/hr, IoB needs >= 2 points with max floored at 1 U, bolus marker radius 4 dp / min spacing 20 dp / stagger 18 dp / base offset 16 dp / stagger cap (0.25*height)/18 dp, min zoom span 15 min, tap proximity 3% of span clamped 60–300 s, tick counts 3/3/4/4/3/7/7/6. Analytics: CGM cross-ref window ±5 min, expected 12 readings/hour, sample stddev (n-1), GMI 3.31 + 0.02392*mean, CV thresholds 36/50, CGM-active thresholds 70/50, TIR quality thresholds 70/50, basal segment cap 2 h, TDD days floor 1. Settings: retention default 7 days clamped 1–30, glucose-range refresh 15 min, glucose-range/safety-limits/alert-thresholds/pump-profile staleness 1 h, analytics staleness 15 min, poll intervals 15 s fast / 300 s medium / 300 s slow, request stagger 500 ms, network failure threshold 2, DB row caps 2000 (chart CGM/IoB/basal), 500 (chart bolus), 50000 (analytics 'All'), home bolus rows 5. Thresholds: defaults 55/70/180/250, clamp 20–500, bolus cap 25 U, glucose bounds 20–500.

5. Two Wear/watch touchpoints appear inside this scope but their implementations live elsewhere (wear-device / watchface modules, presumably another mapping pass): GlucoseFormat is explicitly written as pure Kotlin "so the watch surface can mirror it" and its mmol fixture is pinned against the watch's GlucoseDisplayUtils.formatGlucose; relativeAgeLabel is likewise "reusable by the watch/complication surfaces". Any Swift port must keep the phone and Watch formatters byte-identical for the same stored mg/dL value.

6. Placeholder surfaces that exist as routes but have no content today: TirDetailScreen, InsulinDetailScreen, AlertHistoryScreen (each renders a single "coming in Story 31.x" line). detail/DashboardCard.kt is a built, unused component. presentation/navigation/PlaceholderScreen.kt is likewise unused by the live graph.

7. E2E/test hooks that encode intended behavior and are worth preserving as accessibility identifiers in Swift: connection_status, backend_status, plugin_indicator_<brand>, glucose_hero_value, glucose_hero_trend, hero_iob / hero_basal / hero_battery / hero_reservoir, staleness_badge (zero nodes on a fresh screen — an explicit invariant), glucose_chart, chart_empty_state, expand_chart_detail, period_chip_<label>, tir_bar, tir_quality_label, tir_period_chip_<label>, tir_target_range, cgm_stats_card, cgm_stats_period_<label>, insulin_summary_card, insulin_period_<label>, insulin_stacked_bar, insulin_detail_stats, insulin_category_breakdown, recent_boluses_card, bolus_period_<label>, expand_bolus_detail, view_all_boluses, bolus_history_list, bolus_history_period_<label>, plugin_card_<id>, dashboard_card_<title>, detail_scaffold_<title>, insecure_http_banner, insecure_http_confirm.

ports_cleanly.ios_approach: SwiftUI `ScrollView { LazyVStack(spacing: 0) }` with `.refreshable { await vm.refreshData(); await mealVM.refresh() }` (native pull-to-refresh, no PullToRefreshBox equivalent needed), `.safeAreaPadding` 16pt leading/trailing/top and 88pt bottom, explicit 12pt `Spacer`/padding between cards, and the FAB in a `.overlay(alignment:)` on the ScrollView container rather than inside the scroll content. `onSizeChanged` → `GeometryReader`/`onGeometryChange(for: CGSize.self)` to clamp the draggable FAB. Android's ON_RESUME-minus-first-resume meal refetch → `.onChange(of: scenePhase)` filtering `.active` with a `hasAppeared` flag. The footer line and per-card empty states are plain conditional views. Every card renders unconditionally with its own empty string, exactly as today.

ports_cleanly.capability: Status icon row (BLE / sync / backend reachability)
ports_cleanly.ios_approach: An `HStack` of 16pt symbols with `.accessibilityIdentifier("connection_status")` / `"backend_status"`. SF Symbols mapping: sync-healthy → `arrow.up.arrow.down` (an exact match for Material's SwapVert, preserving the deliberate 'not a cloud' distinction); pending → `arrow.triangle.2.circlepath` over `cloud`; error/not-synced → `cloud.slash`; reachable → `checkmark.icloud` is off-limits (implies iCloud) so use `cloud` + a `checkmark.circle.fill` badge or a custom symbol; unreachable/offline → `cloud.slash`. Bluetooth has no SF Symbol at all — ship a custom SF Symbol set (six variants: connected / searching / plain / disabled) in the asset catalog. The three-mood colour semantics (primary/tertiary/error), the 4pt icon-to-text gap, labelSmall text in matching colour, the 12pt spacers, and the 'connected and disconnected show NO text' rule all transfer verbatim. `backendConfigured` gating hides both cloud indicators in BLE-only mode.

ports_cleanly.capability: Backend-reachability derivation (NetworkStatus)
ports_cleanly.ios_approach: `NWPathMonitor` replaces ConnectivityManager's default-network callback; `path.status == .satisfied` maps to device-online and deliberately does NOT require `path.isExpensive`/validated-internet, preserving the LAN-only-counts-as-online decision. The two-consecutive-transport-failure counter moves into a `URLSession` delegate or an async interceptor wrapping every request, incrementing only on `URLError` transport codes (`.cannotConnectToHost`, `.timedOut`, `.cannotFindHost`, `.networkConnectionLost`) and resetting on any HTTP response including 4xx/5xx. Use an actor or `OSAllocatedUnfairLock` for the counter (URLSession completions are concurrent, same hazard as OkHttp's dispatcher). Offline still takes precedence over unreachable. No health endpoint is introduced.

ports_cleanly.capability: Active-plugin brand indicators
